minutes.headline: ZBA granted a special permit for Bright Eyed's food-kit office at 3 Lancaster Ave, then a conditional permit for a rebuild at 30 Johnson St.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard two special permit applications. Bright Eyed, a nonprofit that packs weekend food kits for students, was granted a permit for office and packing space in the Village Center District after supportive public comment. A permit to rebuild a home at 30 Johnson Street, torn down before zoning approval, was granted on condition that a full-size site plan showing the setbacks is reviewed.

attendees.role: member filling in for Lisa Normandin; reads applications

public_comment.stated_role: resident, school committee member, speaking for himself
public_comment.topic: Supported Bright Eyed, citing family need and its quick help when the schools could not serve meals on a half day.

public_comment.stated_role: president of Lunenburg Village, former owner of 3 Lancaster Ave
public_comment.topic: Fully supported the use of the building as a good transformation for the town center.
Said renting to Bright Eyed is a chance to give back to the community.
Applicant said her neighbors have supported the Johnson Street project; no other public comment came through Zoom.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for Bright Eyed to operate in the Village Center District at 3 Lancaster Avenue.

Issue a special permit to construct a home on the pre-existing non-conforming parcel at 30 Johnson Street, on condition that a full-size site plan showing the existing and new structures and setbacks is submitted and approved by the chair and building inspector.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to grant the Johnson Street permit conditionally, rather than continue the hearing two weeks, if a larger plan with setbacks is reviewed.
The applicant was told to bring one full-size copy of the plan to the building department, preferably within the 14-day filing window.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a conditional special permit to build a home at 30 Johnson Street, on a plan showing setbacks.
The board approved the Bright Eyed special permit for 3 Lancaster Avenue in the Village Center District, after public comment in support.
The board chose to grant the Johnson Street permit conditionally instead of continuing the hearing two weeks.
The Johnson Street applicant was told to bring one full-size plan to the building department, preferably within the 14-day filing window.

why_it_matters: The Johnson Street rebuild goes ahead only if the chair and building inspector approve a full-size plan showing the setbacks, which is the step that decides whether the permit takes effect.
Bright Eyed's permit allows a nonprofit that packs weekend food kits for students to use office and packing space in the town center; the minutes record no budget items.
